chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn Abi Hamza from Abu Baseer who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying, and he had been asked about Al-Tala'a, so he said: 'If it is cooked until two (parts) of it evaporate and one remains, then it is Halal, and whatever is less than that, there is no goodness in it.'

key_terms.الطَّلَاء: Evaporated grape juice, a specific type of sweetener or drink

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on cooked grape juice (Tala'a) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the specific metric for transforming grape juice into a permissible sweetener by requiring two-thirds evaporation, a standard derived from the need to distinguish it from wine (khamr) which becomes intoxicating if not sufficiently reduced. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling highlights the practical application of the principle that sufficient cooking removes the intoxicating quality, thereby making the residue lawful for consumption as a food ingredient rather than a beverage.
